discovery: Dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated electron systems

nominees.name: Antoine Georges
nominees.affiliation: Collège de France, Paris, France, and Flatiron Institute, New York, USA

subfield: Theoretical condensed matter physics / strongly correlated electrons
motivation: Vollhardt (with Metzner) showed that the lattice problem of interacting electrons becomes exactly local in infinite dimensions. Georges and Kotliar then turned this into dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), which maps the problem onto a self-consistent quantum impurity model. For the first time this gave a controlled, non-perturbative description of the Mott metal-insulator transition. It treats quasiparticles and Hubbard bands within one framework. Combined with density-functional theory, DMFT became a predictive first-principles method for materials where band theory fails: transition-metal oxides, f-electron systems such as plutonium, iron-based superconductors, and iron itself at the conditions of Earth's core. Experiments have confirmed its predictions in photoemission, optics and high-pressure studies. DMFT changed condensed-matter theory from a collection of model ideas into quantitative, materials-specific understanding of correlated matter. It is now used worldwide, and it is the conceptual basis for designing quantum materials.
